near_miss.lead: ON risa tunguna bindr ~ Ved. jihvā baddhā 'bound tongue' (*dn̥ǵʰwéh₂- + *bʰendʰ-)
near_miss.why_not: Exact cognate pair, but the contexts are not congruent: in the Þiðreks saga a giant's cut-out tongue is tied to a horse's tail as a token (the tongue-token motif); in AVŚ 5.30 the tongue is 'bound' in a magical sense (speech held back) in a healing charm. Tongue-binding as a curse (Gk katadesmoi) is not what the Norse passage is doing. Only one Indo-Iranian hit for the pair in the index, so it isn't a formula there either.

ON dragon-fight (ljósta á hǫfuð orminum) vs Cato's ham recipe (nec tinia nec uermes tangent): the shared items are *wr̥mi- and a 'touch' verb, the verbs aren't cognate, and the contexts are unrelated. ljósta isn't the *gʷʰen- of the dragon-slaying formula.

near_miss.lead: hǫggr af hǫfuð ormsins 'hews off the serpent's head'
near_miss.why_not: The partner is about cutting basil (falcula secueris). Nothing shared beyond 'cut'. The Norse is ordinary saga prose of dragon-slaying with non-inherited verbs (hǫggva).

The partner φέρουσαν is 'road leading to' in a priestly rite, which isn't congruent. Gk νίκην φέρεσθαι is a parallel idiom, but its noun isn't cognate with sigr (*seǵʰ-), and carrying off a prize is generic.

anchors: xcl:MH_1_2_11_Agathangelos ed. page 1484 - PDF page 190 (word id 33376) (w1/2)
near_miss.lead: hans namn man uppi vera ... meðan veroldin stendr 'his name will live while the world stands' (imperishable-fame theme)
near_miss.why_not: Partners only share *h₁nómn̥ in naming formulas: the Armenian quotes Isaiah 9:6 'his name was called' and OE Finnsburh has 'Sigeferð is min nama'. 'Name lasting while the world stands' is a widespread Christian-medieval phrase, and the slab has no cognate fame formula for it.

near_miss.lead: sleep (*swep-) + secret lover lying with a woman: ON sofnuð ... ligr hjá henni ~ AV lover's sleep charm svapantu jñātayaḥ
near_miss.why_not: The themes are congruent: AVŚ 4.5 is a charm that puts a household to sleep for a lover's visit, and in Þiðreks saga the queen asleep in a garden is visited by an elf (Hǫgni's conception). But the shared material is only the everyday verb 'sleep'. There is no shared wording or figure: the AV is a polyptoton litany of svaptu, the ON a narrative sentence.

near_miss.lead: sverð bítr eigi hǫrund 'sword does not bite his skin' (invulnerability)
near_miss.why_not: The partner is an oracle passage that shares only *kret- (harðr ~ κράτος), with no congruence. Weapons 'biting' (*bʰeyd-) is a Germanic-internal idiom (ON bíta, OE bītan) with no non-Germanic cognate collocation in the slab.

near_miss.lead: sword bites helm, byrnie and shield as if it cut cloth (bítr ... sem hann sníði klæði)
near_miss.why_not: The MBh partner is a fire simile (dagdhā, agninā). The two similes differ and share no cognate material. The Norse is a romance-style cliché.

near_miss.lead: fá vápn bíta á honum (horn-hard skin, invulnerable hero) ~ bhittvā (*bʰeyd-)
near_miss.why_not: bhid- 'split' (the target pierced at the svayaṃvara) and bíta 'bite (of weapons)' are cognate, but the contexts aren't congruent: an archery feat versus an invulnerable hero. binda ~ bandhuḥ in the second MBh partner is unrelated ('kinsman in the other world').

near_miss.lead: 'held the dog in its fore-feet': ON biǫrninn tók ... hund ... með sínum fyrrum fótum ~ Od. 19.228 ἐν προτέροισι πόδεσσι κύων ἔχε (ἐλλόν)
near_miss.why_not: The match is striking: dog + fore-feet (fótr ~ πούς; fyrri ~ πρότερος from the *pro/*pr̥- comparative with different suffixes), plus a hold/take verb in an animal-grip scene. But I reject it: (1) the roles are reversed (Homer's dog holds the fawn, the Norse bear holds the dog); (2) the verbs aren't cognate (taka vs ἔχω); (3) 'fore-feet' is the generic anatomical expression in every language (cf. ON fyrri fǿtr elsewhere, Lat. pedes priores); (4) the Odyssey line describes a brooch image, the Norse a bear-baiting episode. In the Greek index προτερ- + πόδ- occurs only at Od. 19.228, but that is a function of genre, not of formula.

error.correct_reading: risi 'giant' (PGmc *wrisan-/*risan-), not connected to rise or wipe; better left unmapped
error.evidence: Formal resemblance only: the context is a giant (risans blóð), and risi has no accepted link to *wers-.

error.correct_reading: φᾶρος 'cloak, cloth' has no secure IE etymology (probably a loan); it should be unmapped
error.evidence: The context is a woven cloak (ἐξυφήναντες). The given etyma are homophone guesses.

error.evidence: Context: որդի տուաւ մեզ. The same error recurs in the Łazar Parpecʻi passage (տուաւ շնորհ 'grace was given').
